name: redis_get
description: Get the value of a string key. Returns NULL if the key does not exist.

name: redis_set
description: Set the value of a string key.

name: redis_mget
description: Get multiple values in one round-trip. Keys are passed as a comma-separated string; values come back comma-separated in the same order, with an empty entry for each missing key so positions line up. Ambiguous when values contain commas or are empty strings: prefer redis_mget_list.

name: redis_mget_list
description: Get multiple values in one round-trip, typed: takes the keys as a VARCHAR[] and returns a VARCHAR[] of the same length, with NULL for each missing key. Values containing commas or empty strings stay unambiguous. DuckDB 2.0 build.

name: redis_hget
description: Get the value of a hash field. Returns NULL if the key or field does not exist.

name: redis_hset
description: Set the value of a hash field. Returns the number of fields added as a BIGINT: 1 for a new field, 0 when an existing field is overwritten.

name: redis_hgetall
description: List all (field, value) pairs of a hash as a table.

name: redis_hgetall_map
description: All fields and values of a hash as a MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR) — one value per row, so it works per row in a SELECT (redis_hgetall is a table function). An empty map when the key does not exist. DuckDB 2.0 build.

name: redis_hscan
description: Cursor-paginated scan of a hash's fields. Returns 'next_cursor:field1=value1,...'; re-pass the cursor until it comes back as '0'. Ambiguous when fields or values contain ',' or '='; prefer redis_hscan_page.

name: redis_hscan_page
description: One HSCAN step over a hash's fields, typed: returns STRUCT(cursor VARCHAR, entries MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)). Re-pass the cursor until it comes back as '0'. DuckDB 2.0 build.

name: redis_hscan_over_scan
description: For every key matching a SCAN pattern, run HSCAN and emit (key, field, value) rows, following both cursors to the end. Matching keys that are not hashes are skipped. The high-throughput discovery primitive for migration / analysis.

name: redis_lpush
description: Push a value onto the head of a list. Returns the length of the list after the push as a BIGINT.

name: redis_lrange
description: Get a range from a list as a comma-separated string. Ambiguous when elements contain commas; prefer redis_lrange_list.

name: redis_lrange_list
description: Get a range from a list as a VARCHAR[]. start and stop are zero-based and inclusive; negative values count from the end, so 0, -1 is the whole list. An empty list when the key does not exist. DuckDB 2.0 build.

name: redis_lrange_table
description: Get a range from a list as a table — one row per element, with `index` (the element's position in the list) and `value`. In the DuckDB 2.0 build `index` is the real list position, also for a non-zero or negative start; earlier builds numbered rows from 0.

name: redis_del
description: Delete a key. Returns TRUE if the key existed and was removed.

name: redis_exists
description: Check whether a key exists.

name: redis_type
description: Get the Redis type of a key (string / list / hash / set / zset / stream / none).

name: redis_scan
description: Cursor-paginated SCAN of the keyspace, one page per call. Returns 'next_cursor:keys_csv'. Iterate by re-passing the returned cursor until it comes back as '0'. Prefer redis_scan_page for a typed result.

name: redis_scan_page
description: One SCAN step over the keys matching a pattern, typed: returns STRUCT(cursor VARCHAR, keys VARCHAR[]). Re-pass the cursor until it comes back as '0'; a key may appear in more than one page. DuckDB 2.0 build.

name: redis_keys
description: List all keys matching a pattern as a table, one row per key. Built on SCAN, not KEYS: it follows the cursor page by page until the keyspace is exhausted, so it doesn't block the server — but it always walks the whole keyspace. Use redis_scan to page manually.

name: redis_expire
description: Set a key's time-to-live in seconds. Returns TRUE if the TTL was set, FALSE if the key does not exist.

name: redis_expireat
description: Expire a key at an absolute Unix timestamp (seconds). Returns TRUE if the expiry was set, FALSE if the key does not exist.

name: redis_ttl
description: Remaining time-to-live in seconds. Returns -1 if the key has no expiry and -2 if the key does not exist.

name: redis_command
description: Run any Redis command, given as a VARCHAR[] of the command name and its arguments — sets, sorted sets, counters, streams and anything else without a dedicated function. Strings and integers come back as text, nil as NULL, and array replies (also RESP3 maps and sets, flattened) as JSON arrays. Error replies raise an error. The connection is closed afterwards instead of being pooled, since the command may change its state (SELECT, CLIENT, SUBSCRIBE). DuckDB 2.0 build.
